content.text: Prop firm rules change often. This guide reflects the firm's published rules when it was last updated (see the date above). Always confirm current rules on the firm's official site before you trade your evaluation.

TopStep is one of the oldest funded futures programs in the industry. Its Trading Combine is a single-phase evaluation that looks simpler than FTMO's two-phase structure — but Topstep itself reports that only 16.8% of Combines were completed in 2025 (why most traders fail prop firm evaluations). Most traders who fail do not fail because of poor strategy. They fail because of behavioral mistakes that a better understanding of the rules would prevent.

The short answer to how to pass the TopStep evaluation: treat every rule as a hard boundary, not a guideline. The three rules that matter most are the Maximum Loss Limit (it trails your end-of-day balance, which surprises many traders at the worst moment), the Daily Loss Limit (optional, if you add it at checkout) and the 55% consistency target (a big day doesn't fail you, but it raises your profit target).

This guide explains every TopStep rule with concrete numbers, walks through the most common failure patterns, and shows you how to structure your daily trading routine to stay inside the parameters from day one.

The TopStep Consistency Target: Math With Real Numbers

Topstep's consistency target works differently from most prop firm rules. One exceptional day does not end your Combine — it moves the finish line. If your best day is more than 55% of your total profit, your new profit target becomes your best day divided by 0.55.
The Formula
Best-day share = Best Day P&L ÷ Total Net Profit. Adjusted target (if above 55%) = Best Day ÷ 0.55

rows: Target met after a few more sessions

content.text: The important insight: a big day costs you time, not the account. A $1,900 day on the 50K means you need $3,455 in total profit instead of $3,000. The danger is what traders do next — oversizing to "get it over with" is how a raised target turns into a Maximum Loss Limit breach. Know your adjusted target in real time, not after you think you've passed.
After any unusually strong day, check your best-day share immediately. If it is above 45%, keep your normal size and stop trying to add another big day — let your total catch up steadily.
How the Maximum Loss Limit Works — And When It Catches Traders Off Guard
The Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) is the most misunderstood mechanic in the Trading Combine. On the $50,000 account it is $2,000, and it trails your end-of-day balance:

items: Start: balance = $50,000 → floor = $48,000
You close the day at $51,000 → floor rises to $49,000
You close the next day at $52,000 → floor rises to $50,000
Intraday spikes don't move it: if you were up to $52,800 during the session but closed at $52,000, the floor is based on the $52,000 close
If you now lose $2,000 → balance hits $50,000 → you are exactly at the floor → the Combine ends
Where the MLL stops trailing is defined in Topstep's help center — check it for your account size

content.text: The dangerous part: while the floor is trailing, every dollar you add at the close also raises the floor by a dollar. Traders with a fast start often feel more pressure, not less — the floor has followed them up and left them with the same $2,000 buffer they started with.
Common Failure Patterns in the TopStep Trading Combine
Pattern 1: Trading High-Impact News Without a Plan

NFP, FOMC decisions and CPI releases can move NQ and ES violently in seconds, and a slipped stop can take out your daily loss limit in a single trade. Check Topstep's help center for any rules on your account type around major releases, keep an economic calendar open every day, and decide before the session whether you will be flat or sized down during those minutes.
Pattern 2: Increasing Position Size After a Good Day

This is one of the most common account-ending sequences: a trader has 4-5 good days in a row, feels confident, doubles their contract size on day 6, and takes a larger-than-normal loss. The loss itself may not violate the daily limit — but it triggers revenge trading, which does. Journal every session and flag your best days as high-risk behavioral triggers for the following session.
Pattern 3: Ignoring the Consistency Percentage

Traders often think they've hit the profit target and stop tracking — without noticing the consistency target has raised it. The fix is simple: check your best-day share every morning before your session begins. If it is above 55%, calculate your adjusted target (best day ÷ 0.55) and plan the remaining sessions around it.
Pattern 4: Letting Losing Days Compound

A single losing day does not fail a Combine. But traders who push through two or three bad days in a row — trying to 'make it back' — are the ones who eventually breach the Maximum Loss Limit when the buffer is already stretched. Set a personal daily stop at 60-70% of your daily loss limit and close the platform when you hit it. No exceptions.
Daily Routine for Passing the TopStep Trading Combine
Traders who pass on their first or second attempt follow a structured daily routine. Here is the framework:

items: Morning (before market open): check the economic calendar for high-impact releases and note their times
Calculate position sizing: maximum contracts so that 3 consecutive losses stay within your personal daily stop
Check your best-day share: know whether your profit target has moved
Set a daily profit target: a ceiling that prevents the Big Day Trap — stop trading when you reach it
Set your personal daily stop: about $600-$700 on the 50K if you chose the $1,000 Daily Loss Limit (60-70% of it)
During session: log every trade with emotional state and plan-compliance tag immediately after close
After session: update your journal with end-of-day balance, Maximum Loss Limit floor and best-day share
Weekly review: 30 minutes on Sunday to identify the worst decision of the week and set one behavioral goal

Frequently Asked Questions About Passing TopStep

faqItems.q: How long does it take to pass the TopStep Trading Combine?
faqItems.a: It depends on your strategy and your discipline: some traders pass in a week, others take months. Check Topstep's help center for the current Combine terms. Do not rush it — rushed Combines are where oversizing and Maximum Loss Limit breaches happen.

faqItems.q: What happens if I hit a loss limit on TopStep?
faqItems.a: Breaching the Maximum Loss Limit ends the Combine. If you added the optional Daily Loss Limit, check Topstep's help center for exactly what happens when you reach it. Either way, a personal daily stop well below the limit keeps you out of that situation.

faqItems.q: Does TopStep have a consistency rule?
faqItems.a: Yes, a consistency target. On the Combine your best day should be no more than 55% of your total profit (updated September 2026). If it is higher, the Combine is not failed: your profit target rises to your best day divided by 0.55. Zentrade shows your best day's share of profit live.

faqItems.q: Can I trade micro futures on TopStep?
faqItems.a: Yes, micro contracts such as MES and MNQ are popular in the Combine because they make it easier to size positions inside the loss limits. Check Topstep's help center for the full list of permitted products and contract limits.

faqItems.q: Is TopStep's Maximum Loss Limit based on intraday or end-of-day balance?
faqItems.a: End-of-day. On the 50K Combine the Maximum Loss Limit is $2,000 and trails your end-of-day balance, so the floor starts at $48,000 and only moves when you close the day at a new high balance — intraday spikes don't move it.

faqItems.q: How does TopStep compare to FTMO for futures traders?
faqItems.a: TopStep has one evaluation phase; FTMO's classic challenge has two. Topstep uses a 55% consistency target that raises your profit target; FTMO's 2-Step has no consistency rule and a static 10% max loss, while its 1-Step has a 50% Best Day Rule. Pick the structure that fits how you trade.
